title: The Wild Crown Anew
premise: Yara Villalobos, a runaway apprentice hiding in the smuggler's roads of the Thornfell mountains, discovers their own face in a century-old book of prophecies — and learns that their late mentor bound them at birth to an ancient covenant between the human free cities and the fading fae realm of Thornfell. Hunted by the usurper King Aldric's witch-finders and reluctantly allied with Serah, a disgraced knight sent to capture them, Yara must gather three shattered crown-shards held by hostile factions on both sides of the veil. As Aldric's armies march and the covenant's collapse begins poisoning the land itself, Yara realizes the prophecy demands a sacrifice they never agreed to. In the end, Yara refuses the prophecy's terms entirely: by sharing the burden of the reforged crown with Serah and the fae queen's exiled daughter, they forge a new covenant that costs power instead of lives — though it leaves Yara mortal, magicless, and finally free to choose who they are.
about_author: Sebastian Blackwood is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in borderlands, bargains, and the people history forgets.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Almanac
chapters.summary: Yara Villalobos guides contraband through the Thornfell passes by night, keeping their hedge-magic hidden even from the smugglers who trust them. A routine delivery goes wrong when a dying courier presses a sealed book into their hands. POV: Yara. Beat: wary competence cracked open by fate's intrusion.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Holed up in a waystation, Yara opens the book and finds a prophecy written a century ago describing tonight's date — and themselves, down to a scar on their knuckles. Their dead mentor's handwriting fills the margins. POV: Yara. Beat: dread and vertigo as invisibility dies.

chapters.title: The Knight at the Ford
chapters.summary: Serah Dain, knight-captain stripped of rank for questioning King Aldric, is ordered to hunt the 'prophesied vessel.' She intercepts Yara at a river ford but hesitates when she sees the witch-finders burning a village behind her. POV: Serah. Beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: What the Mentor Buried
chapters.summary: Fleeing together out of necessity, Yara deciphers the margins: their mentor bound them at birth as the covenant's living key, then hid them to spare them. The first crown-shard lies beneath the drowned chapel of Vaelmoor. POV: Yara. Beat: grief curdling into anger.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: King Aldric, in his capital, weighs conquest against the failing covenant that keeps his armies fed; he has decided to seize the shards and rule both realms by force. His spymaster warns him the prophecy cannot be controlled. POV: Aldric. Beat: cold ambition presented sympathetically.

chapters.title: Drowned Bells
chapters.summary: At Vaelmoor's flooded chapel, Yara and Serah dive for the first shard while witch-finders close in. Serah saves Yara from drowning, breaking her orders openly. POV: alternating. Beat: trust forged underwater, shard won at cost of exposure.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Waited
chapters.summary: Crossing the veil, they meet Nyssara, exiled daughter of the fae queen, who reveals the second shard was kept by her mother — who now serves Aldric under duress. Nyssara offers alliance for a promise Yara isn't sure they can keep. POV: Yara. Beat: uneasy bargain.

chapters.title: Free Cities, Fenced Hearts
chapters.summary: The trio reaches the free city of Corvane to rally resistance, but the council fears fae entanglement more than Aldric. Serah's old comrades nearly arrest her; Yara's public magic makes them a symbol they never wanted to be. POV: Serah. Beat: politics as slow violence.

chapters.title: A Date With the Dead
chapters.summary: In Corvane's necropolis, Yara performs a rite to question their mentor's ghost and learns the covenant's original price: a life freely given each century. The mentor hid this to protect them, dooming the realms instead. POV: Yara. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness tangled.

chapters.title: Witch-Fire
chapters.summary: Aldric's witch-finders storm Corvane. Yara unleashes magic far beyond their training to cover the evacuation, revealing the full scale of what they are — and drawing Aldric's personal attention. POV: Yara. Beat: power as exhilaration and horror at once.

chapters.title: The Road Neither Map Shows
chapters.summary: Hunted and half-burned, the group takes a smuggler's road only Yara knows, through territory where the failing covenant warps reality. Old debts come due with the mountain itself. POV: Serah. Beat: intimacy kindling between Serah and Yara amid exhaustion.

chapters.title: Mother's Crown
chapters.summary: They infiltrate the fae court where the captive queen holds the second shard. Nyssara confronts her mother; the queen, broken by a century of captivity, gives the shard willingly but warns the third lies inside Aldric himself. POV: Nyssara. Beat: filial love and ruin.

chapters.title: Two Crowns, One Neck
chapters.summary: Serah and Yara admit their feelings the night before the hardest leg, knowing the prophecy may demand one of their deaths. They agree to defy it together or not at all. POV: alternating. Beat: love chosen against duty, tender and doomed-feeling.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Aldric's vanguard burns the mountain villages to starve the resistance. Yara must choose between saving refugees with magic that will burn out their lifespan or preserving strength for the final ritual. They choose the refugees. POV: Yara. Beat: theme made flesh; cost accepted.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: The battered free cities' leaders meet in a ruined keep. Yara, voice scorched from overuse, argues for a new covenant; the council demands proof the old one can be broken without apocalypse. Nyssara demonstrates the land's decay. POV: Serah. Beat: hope argued for, barely won.

chapters.title: The King's Shard
chapters.summary: Aldric wears the third shard fused to his signet ring, and it whispers to him. Alone, he recalls the brother he lost to the last covenant's price, explaining his hunger for control. POV: Aldric. Beat: villain humanized; corruption traced to grief.

chapters.title: Gambit at Greywater
chapters.summary: The resistance ambushes Aldric's army at the Greywater crossing. Serah duels her former second-in-command while Yara slips toward the king's pavilion. The battle is won, but Aldric escapes with the shard — and takes Nyssara hostage. POV: Serah. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Aldric offers a parley: the shard and peace in exchange for Yara's surrender as the covenant's sacrifice. Yara agrees secretly, planning to subvert the ritual from within; Serah discovers the plan and feels betrayed. POV: Yara. Beat: love tested by self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: At the ancient covenant-stone, Aldric forces the ritual early to seize both crowns. The old covenant shatters catastrophically; the veil tears, and wild magic floods the battlefield. Yara seizes the moment to pull all three shards loose. POV: alternating. Beat: climax — everything breaks.

chapters.title: Reforging
chapters.summary: Amid the tearing veil, Yara rejects the prophecy's single-sacrifice design and calls on Serah and Nyssara to share the binding. Three hands on the shards, they reforge the crown as a shared covenant rather than a throne. Aldric, offered a place in it, refuses and falls into the collapsing veil. POV: Yara. Beat: climax resolved by refusal of the false choice.

chapters.title: Mortal Again
chapters.summary: The new covenant holds, but it took Yara's magic as its price. They wake powerless in Corvane, ordinary for the first time since birth, and find the freedom in it. The free cities and fae begin cautious talks. POV: Yara. Beat: quiet aftermath, grief and relief braided.

chapters.title: The Wild Crown Anew
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Yara walks the Thornfell roads as a guide again — no longer hiding, no longer hunted. Serah rides beside them; Nyssara rules a thawing fae court. On the wind, faintly, the mountains seem to say thank you. POV: Yara. Beat: resolution — survival fully paid for, love freely chosen.
